analysis:
Both units are CHANGELOG.md prose only (head lines 555-1132). No executable code, protocol, or configuration changes are visible, so no concrete regression is identified in these units. I checked the release notes for claims that could invalidate threat-model assumptions.

Two-Mac cluster notes (lines 559-805) describe encrypted peer links, authenticated frames, a per-piece authenticated sealed sum that fails the request when a piece does not open, and a same-release requirement between Macs. They also say gates for qualification, memory and native teardown are retained. These statements are consistent with the threat model's plaintext-endpoint and provider-adversary stance, but the implementing code is not in this batch. The cluster feature expands the trust boundary: a peer Mac handles decrypted prompts, and the operator-trusted cluster_runtime registration block feeds coordinator approvals (TB-002, TB-011, T-053/T-054). Next-pass reviewers should confirm that the code gates this, and that the T-056 non-claim of runtime secrecy still holds for peer Macs.

SSD cache notes (lines 898-967) cover concurrent restores, mtime refresh rules, bounded eviction, header caching and the expired-versus-corrupt counter. They say TTL, budget and ownership decisions are unchanged and that complete checkpoints are stored per binary hash. These touch T-041. The notes state that a restart can drop a file whose mtime was not refreshed. They do not show weakened TTL, HMAC naming or AES-GCM, but the source of the cache code was not reviewed here.

CI/release notes (lines 823-845) say the dev-branch lane now signs, notarizes and staples builds like master. They also say dev publication is refused from master and that the final app is checked against the self-updater designated requirement. This is relevant to T-013/T-034 and release-signing trust, and the workflow files are unverified here. The sandbox CLI notes (line 814, 819-821) describe downloading and running the add-on installer over HTTPS, which is the TB-013/T-061 surface, and are documentation only.

The notes also mention the addon hold hardening in the v0.10.4 section, which is consistent with TB-012/T-059/T-060. The needs_deeper_review flag is set because claims in the changelog could not be verified against code, though nothing here is a finding.
